title: Domestic Investors Accumulate BBCA, BBRI, and TLKM Shares Amid MSCI Downgrade Turmoil
body: Between October 16 and 23, 2026, domestic investors accumulated blue-chip stocks amid market turmoil following MSCI's announcement of consultations to downgrade Indonesia from emerging markets to standalone markets. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) recorded the largest overall net buy of Rp 4.36 trillion despite foreign net sell of Rp 5.22 trillion, while PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) posted overall net buys of Rp 1.33 trillion and Rp 1.31 trillion against foreign net sells of Rp 3.26 trillion and Rp 663 billion respectively. The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) plunged 11.57% to 5,185 on October 16 before recovering to close at 5,439 on October 23. Separately, BBCA planned a share buyback on October 19-21, 2026, part of a program approved at its March 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, with management not yet detailing the fund allocation.

title: Popular News Roundup: BBCA Faces Foreign Net Sell Amid MSCI Reclassification Threat, PACK Plans Rp 8.19 Trillion Rights Issue, and DEWA Projected Near 100% Share Price Gain
body: This roundup of five most-read investor.id stories as of Friday (23/10/2026) covers Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), which recorded foreign net sell of Rp 621.42 billion on Thursday (22/10/2026) with its share price falling 1.90% to Rp 5,175, amid MSCI's announced threat of reclassifying the Indonesian stock market. PT Abadi Nusantara Hijau Investama Tbk (PACK), a portfolio company of Haji Isam, plans a rights issue (PMHMETD I) of up to 100 billion new shares worth a maximum of Rp 8.19 trillion to repay loans, purchase DDL shares, and fund working capital for the company and/or its subsidiaries. PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) posted the highest foreign net buy of Rp 360.1 billion among stocks during the MSCI turmoil period of 16–22 October 2026, according to Stockbit Sekuritas. The roundup also includes educational content on living off dividends, advising selection of stocks with a dividend payout ratio above 50% and dividend yield above 4%. Finally, Bakrie Group issuer PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA), with Nirwan Bakrie as beneficial owner, is projected by BRI Danareksa Sekuritas analysts to post a 142.6% net profit jump in 2027 to Rp 1.64 trillion from an estimated Rp 676 billion in 2026, with revenue rising from Rp 7.22 trillion to Rp 11.78 trillion and a buy recommendation with a target price implying a 97% upside.

title: Indonesian Issuers Including BBRI, BBCA, TLKM, JSMR, and AMMN Prepare or Extend Share Buyback Programs
body: Several issuers on the Indonesia Stock Exchange are preparing, continuing, or studying share buyback programs amid a recent correction in the composite stock price index. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) is preparing a second-stage buyback of up to Rp1 trillion, scheduled for 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027 with OJK approval, after realizing about Rp90.37 billion of a Rp500 billion allocation in its previous program. PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) plans to accelerate its regular buyback of up to Rp4 trillion, with more than Rp3 trillion remaining as of 19 October 2026, separately from a completed repurchase of 15,956,199 shares worth Rp36.54 billion at Rp2,290 per share tied to dissenting shareholders of its wholesale fiber connectivity spin-off. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) extended its buyback period from 19-21 October to 19-23 October 2026, with around Rp3.5 trillion realized of a Rp5 trillion program valid until March 2027. PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) is studying a potential buyback without announced value or schedule, while PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) is allocating about Rp1 trillion from internal cash for a buyback running 22 October 2026 to 22 January 2027.

title: Popular News Roundup: Russia Draws Down Gold Reserves, GEMS Pays Interim Dividend, BBCA and BBRI Buybacks, ADMR Dividend Outlook
body: This roundup of five popular investor.id stories covers Bank of Russia's sale of 200,000 troy ounces (6.2 tons) of gold in September 2026, cutting reserves to 72.8 million troy ounces (2,264 tons), the lowest since late 2019, after liquidating about 62 tons since December 2025 to fund the federal deficit. PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk (GEMS), a coal mining issuer of the Sinar Mas Group, pays an interim dividend of US$200 million, or Rp611.93 per share (US$0,034), on 22 October 2026 using a BI middle rate of Rp17,996 per US dollar. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) recorded the largest foreign net buy of Rp448.09 billion on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, closing up 1.4% at Rp5,275, and extended its share buyback to 23 October 2026. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) announced a phase II 2026 buyback of up to Rp1 trillion from internal cash, with treasury stock not exceeding 10% of placed capital. PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR), an affiliate of Boy Thohir, is seen as an accumulation opportunity after its net cash flow turned positive at US$210 million in 2026, with projected 2027 cash flow of US$533 million supporting an estimated Rp127 per share dividend for 2027.

title: Trillions of Rupiah Ready to Enter the Market as 10 Issuers Prepare Rp 18.6 Trillion Share Buybacks, BRI Danareksa Sekuritas Says
body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (BRIDS) notes that at least 10 issuers are preparing share buyback programs totaling up to Rp 18.6 trillion, adding demand-side support amid market volatility. Five new programs worth Rp 4.5 trillion from DSSA, BREN, BRPT, TPIA, and CUAN began between October 19-23, shortly after the market correction on October 16, providing about Rp 1.8 trillion of support per month over 2-3 months. Companies affiliated with Prajogo lead with Rp 3.5 trillion, as BREN, BRPT, TPIA, and CUAN hold 78% of the new program funds, active until December 31, 2026. Large banks have committed Rp 10.1 trillion, or 54% of the total, with BBCA the largest at Rp 5.0 trillion, followed by BBRI at Rp 3.0 trillion, while annual programs from BBCA, TLKM, BMRI, and BBNI run at about Rp 0.9 trillion per month. BRIDS notes that buyback values are maximum limits and actual realization may be smaller.

title: Foreign Investors Record Largest Net Buy in PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Shares at Rp 448.09 Billion
body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) was the top foreign net buy on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) on Wednesday (21/10/2026), with foreign net buy of Rp 448.09 billion in the regular market, and the stock closed up 1.4% at Rp 5,275. BCA has extended its share buyback program until 23 October 2026, from the previous schedule ending 21 October 2026, with the continued buyback running since 19 October 2026. Foreign investors also bought PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS) shares worth Rp 51.1 billion, while the largest foreign net sell hit PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) at Rp 227.4 billion and PT Antam Tbk (ANTM) at Rp 83.1 billion. Overall, foreign investors posted a net buy of Rp 12.49 billion across the IDX, bringing the year-to-date foreign net sell to Rp 92.09 trillion, while the IHSG rose 49.47 points (0.94%) to 5,328.3 with total transaction value of Rp 17.1 trillion.

title: Bank Stocks Rally as Bank Indonesia Holds BI Rate at 5.75%
body: Banking stocks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange rose after Bank Indonesia's October Board of Governors Meeting decided to keep the benchmark rate at 5.75%, below the Bloomberg consensus median of 5.88%. PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk (BBTN) jumped 3.89% to Rp 935 and PT Bank Permata Tbk (BNLI) surged 3.83%, while PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) climbed 1.79% to Rp 2,840. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) added 0.96% to Rp 5,250 and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) gained 0.27% to Rp 3,700. Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia noted that holding the rate with convincing communication on rupiah stability could support banking stocks and the bond market.

title: 10 Issuers Prepare Rp 18.6 Trillion Share Buybacks After IHSG Plunge
body: Ten Indonesian issuers are preparing share buyback programs totaling Rp 18.6 trillion, which BRI Danareksa Sekuritas says should support buying interest amid rising volatility. Five new buybacks worth Rp 4.5 trillion, starting October 19-23, 2026, shortly after the market's sharp correction on October 16, 2026, come from PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN), PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT), PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA), and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN), running through December 31, 2026. Four of these issuers affiliated with businessman Prajogo Pangestu—BREN, BRPT, TPIA, and CUAN—account for about 78 percent of the new funds with a combined Rp 3.5 trillion. Big banks remain the largest overall contributors, committing Rp 10.1 trillion or 54 percent of the total, led by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) with Rp 5 trillion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) with Rp 3 trillion. BRI Danareksa noted the announced buyback values represent maximum limits that may be used.

title: Indonesian Issuers Including Telkom, BCA, BNI, BTN, Adaro Energy, Barito Pacific, TPIA, DSSA, BREN, and CUAN Announce or Review Share Buybacks
body: Several issuers on the Indonesia Stock Exchange are conducting or preparing share buybacks totaling trillions of rupiah amid market turmoil, spanning banking, telecommunications, energy, and petrochemical sectors. PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) is accelerating its buyback with over Rp3 trillion remaining from a Rp4 trillion program approved at its 8 June 2026 RUPST, while PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) extended its buyback to 19-23 October 2026 and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) is running its program through 26 October 2026. PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk (BBTN) is still studying a possible buyback, having previously set aside Rp275 billion in 2020. PT Adaro Energy Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) began buybacks on 20 October 2026, while PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT), PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (TPIA), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), and PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN) each allocated up to Rp1 trillion, with TPIA planning up to 800 million shares at a maximum price of Rp3,000 per share, and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) allocating up to Rp500 billion, all through 31 December 2026. DSSA, BREN, and CUAN were previously fined by the OJK Rp1.5 trillion, Rp500 billion, and Rp100 billion respectively for capital market violations.

title: 91% of Analysts Recommend Buy on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Despite Foreign Net Sell Pressure
body: Foreign investors recorded net sell of PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) shares totaling around Rp1.95 trillion over two trading days, including Rp986.87 billion on Monday (19/10/2026) and Rp966.11 billion on Tuesday (20/10/2026), amid concerns over Indonesia's MSCI market classification. Despite the selling pressure, BBCA shares rose 7.88% to Rp5,200 on Tuesday and gained 0.48% to Rp5,225 in the first session on Wednesday (21/10/2026). UBS research noted BBCA's loan growth accelerated to 10.5% YoY in August 2026, net interest margin recovered to 5.6%-5.7%, and return on equity reached about 24%, recommending Buy with a target price of Rp7,150. Sucor Sekuritas analyst Edward Lowis maintained a Buy rating with a target price of Rp6,800, projecting net profit of Rp55.7 trillion in 2026 and Rp54.8 trillion in 2027, citing a CASA ratio of 84.3% and a cost-to-income ratio of 29.3% in H1-2026. Per Bloomberg consensus, 34 of 37 analysts, or 91.9%, recommend Buy, three or 8.1% recommend Hold, and none recommend Sell.

title: Six Indonesian Issuers Announce New Buyback Programs Totaling Up to Rp4.6 Trillion Amid Market Volatility
body: Six issuers announced new share buyback plans amid capital market turmoil: PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT), PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN), PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA), and PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) each allocated up to Rp1 trillion, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) up to Rp500 billion, and PT Paramita Bangun Sarana Tbk (PBSA) Rp100 billion, for a combined maximum of Rp4.6 trillion. Separately, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) resumed buybacks on October 19–21, 2026 under its Rp5 trillion program approved at the March 12, 2026 annual general meeting, while ADRO and AADI of the Boy Thohir group began phased buybacks on October 20, 2026, each with a Rp5 trillion ceiling. TLKM is accelerating its Rp4 trillion buyback approved at the June 8, 2026 RUPST, with remaining allocation above Rp3 trillion as of October 19. The buybacks without prior shareholder approval are permitted under OJK Regulation No. 13 of 2023 and an OJK letter dated September 9, 2026 covering significantly fluctuating market conditions.

title: Domestic Demand Absorbs Heavy Foreign Selling in BBCA as IHSG Rebounds 5.65%
body: The IHSG rebounded 5.65% to 5,278 with total market transaction value of Rp 26.5 trillion, after falling 3.64% on Monday to 4,996, driven mainly by four large banks rising more than 5%. Foreign net sell continued at Rp 2.19 trillion, dominated by BBCA (Rp 966 billion), followed by ISAT, MDKA, and ICBP, while TLKM saw a foreign net buy of Rp 255 billion and jumped 16.38%. BBCA led transaction value at Rp 6 trillion, or 22.68% of the market total, despite being the most heavily foreign-sold stock, indicating domestic demand absorbed the foreign outflow. Maybank Sekuritas also noted upcoming dividend catalysts, including AADI's potential special dividend from the completed Kestrel divestment (net proceeds around US$735 million), SCMA's interim dividend of Rp 8.4 per share with cum date October 27, and DMAS's interim dividend of Rp 29 per share with cum date October 28.

title: Popular News Roundup: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Shares at Cheapest Valuation in 10 Years, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Dividend, and MSCI-Driven Market Turmoil
body: This roundup of five popular investor.id stories is led by a rare event for PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), whose shares plunged 6.86% to Rp 4,820 on Monday (19/10/2026), hitting auto rejection bottom (ARB) and their lowest level in five years, with 382.92 million shares traded across 81,606 transactions worth Rp 1.86 trillion, leaving the stock at its cheapest valuation in at least 10 years. PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) posted first-half 2026 net profit of Rp 30.4 trillion, up 24% year-on-year and reaching 53% of FY26F estimates, distributed dividends of about Rp 44.47 trillion from 2025 net profit of Rp 56.3 trillion, and set a 2026 interim dividend of Rp 6.16 trillion, or Rp 66 per share. Amid pressure on the IHSG, which fell more than 5% on Monday (19/10/2026) after dropping about 11.6% on Friday (16/10/2026) due to MSCI-related turmoil, Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia recommended seven fundamentally strong stocks: TLKM, ASII, PGAS, ANTM, PTBA, BBCA, and BMRI. Jusuf Hamka, also known as Babah Alun, said PT Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada Tbk (CMNP) has risen amid recent market volatility despite a year-to-date correction of 440 points (29.93%), while Danantara Indonesia confirmed the merger of its four investment management companies into PT Mandiri Manajemen Investasi (MMI), which will be followed by human resource transformation, governance strengthening, technology development, and improved investment management standards.

title: Foreign Investors Net Sell Rp 2.19 Trillion as IHSG Jumps 5.65%, with TLKM Quietly Accumulated
body: Foreign investors posted a jumbo net sell of Rp 2.19 trillion across all markets on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) on Tuesday (20/10/2026), even as the IHSG surged 282.2 points (5.65%) to close at 5,278.8. The largest foreign net sells hit PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) at Rp 966.1 billion, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) at Rp 355.39 billion, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) at Rp 269.8 billion, PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) at Rp 125.6 billion, PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) at Rp 117.8 billion, and PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (ICBP) at Rp 107.3 billion. In contrast, the biggest foreign net buys went to PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) at Rp 254.9 billion and PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) at Rp 98.49 billion. Pilarmas Investindo Sekuritas attributed the rebound to regulator efforts to restore investor confidence after MSCI warned Indonesia's status could be downgraded from emerging market to standalone market, with the IDX designing a new IHSG calculation mechanism excluding issuers with high shareholding concentration (HSC) following a meeting between the IDX and MSCI. Year-to-date foreign net sell has risen to Rp 92.1 trillion, while total market transaction value reached Rp 26.3 trillion.

title: Big Bank Stocks Rebound After MSCI Pressure as PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk (BBTN) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) Review Buyback Options
body: Large-cap banking stocks rebounded on Tuesday (20/10/2026) after pressure from the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) announcement, with the IHSG rising 5.65% to 5,278. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) gained 9.84% to Rp 2,790, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) rose 9.82% to Rp 3,690, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) climbed 8.78% to Rp 3,220, and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) advanced 7.88% to Rp 5,200, despite foreign net sell of Rp 2.13 trillion led by BBCA at Rp 966.11 billion. PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk (BBTN) is reviewing a buyback option, having previously allocated Rp 275 billion for a buyback in 2020, while BBNI is considering extending its buyback period scheduled to end on 26 October 2026, subject to capital adequacy and shareholder interests.

title: IHSG Jumps 5.65% as Indonesia Bourse Moves to Counter MSCI Downgrade Threat
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rose 5.65%, or 282.28 points, to 5,278.89 on Tuesday (20/10), rebounding after falling more than 15% in two days following MSCI's proposal to downgrade Indonesia from Emerging Market to Standalone Market status. The rebound reflected positive market response to initiatives by the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) to meet MSCI standards, including changes to the Auto Reject Bottom (ARB) stock limit, plans to remove High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) stocks from the IHSG calculation, and greater transparency on affiliated shareholders of issuers. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) anchored the rally, rising 9.84% and 7.88% and contributing 36.95 and 34.73 index points respectively. Total transaction value reached Rp26.54 trillion with 694 gainers, 111 decliners, and 33 unchanged stocks, while Phintraco Sekuritas analysts warned foreign selling pressure remained high and volatility could persist, with the IHSG potentially testing the 5,300-5,400 level.

title: Two Bank Issuers Announce Share Buyback Plans as Indonesian Market Rebounds After MSCI Review Shock
body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) announced its third share buyback of 2026, running from October 19 to 21, 2026, under a maximum budget of Rp 5 trillion approved at its March 2026 annual shareholders meeting, with prior buybacks executed in April and June 2026. PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk (BBTN) said it is studying a buyback as one corporate action option, weighing financial condition, capital adequacy, expansion funding needs, and regulatory requirements, according to President Director Nixon Napitupulu. The announcements came after MSCI's consideration of downgrading the Indonesian stock market from emerging market to standalone market sent the IHSG down 14.91% in a week to 5,185.10 on October 16, 2026, followed by a 3.64% drop to 4,996.6 on October 19 and a 5.65% rebound to 5,278.89 on October 20. BBCA shares fell 6.86% to Rp 4,820 on the announcement day, hitting the Auto Reject Bottom (ARB) limit of 7%, before rising 7.88% to Rp 5,200 on October 20, while BBTN gained 5.88% to Rp 900; analyst Nafan Aji Gusta of Mirae Asset Sekuritas attributed the recovery to extreme oversold technical conditions rather than the buyback announcements.

title: Indonesian Issuers Announce 59 Share Buyback Programs Through 2026, Including BBCA, DSSA, and CUAN
body: A roundup of Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) disclosures through 20 October 2026 records 59 share buyback programs announced by issuers during 2026, of which 12 are completed and 46 remain active. The largest programs include PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) with a maximum of Rp8 trillion, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) and PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) at Rp5 trillion each, PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) at Rp4 trillion, and PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) at Rp3.5 trillion. Four Prajogo Pangestu-affiliated issuers—PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT), PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA), PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN), and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN)—announced new programs starting 19 October 2026 totaling Rp3.5 trillion in maximum funds, while PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) and PT Bank BTPN Syariah Tbk (BTPS) each set Rp1 trillion. Other issuers with buyback programs include PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI), PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (KLBF), PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (ERAA), PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA), PT Bangun Kosambi Sukses Tbk (CBDK), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI), PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk (BNGA), PT Bank Nationalnobu Tbk (NOBU), PT Allo Bank Indonesia Tbk (BBHI), PT Steel Pipe Industry Indonesia Tbk (ISSP), PT Jasuindo Tiga Perkasa Tbk (JTPE), PT TBS Energi Utama Tbk (TOBA), and PT Elnusa Tbk (ELSA), with maximum values representing allocated limits rather than realized purchases.

title: Foreign Investors Net Sell Rp 1.97 Trillion in Big Bank Stocks BBCA, BBRI, BMRI on IDX
body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 1.97 trillion in session I trading on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) on Tuesday (20/10/2026), led by selling in three major bank stocks. Foreign investors sold PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) shares worth Rp 1.02 trillion (206.8 million shares), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) shares worth Rp 245 billion (91.4 million shares), and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) shares worth Rp 208.9 billion (58.2 million shares), based on average prices in session I. The selling occurred in the regular market even as the stocks rallied, with BBCA up 4.25% to Rp 5,025, BBRI up 8.27% to Rp 2,750, and BMRI up 8.93% to Rp 3,660. Year to date, BBCA has fallen 37.7%, BBRI 24.8%, and BMRI 28.2%, while over the past month the stocks declined 20.2%, 16.9%, and 14%, respectively.

title: Buyback Plans by Listed Issuers Not Yet Enough to Lift IHSG, Investors Advised to Wait and See
body: Market commentary from Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia's Head of Investment Specialist Fath Aliansyah Budiman suggests buyback plans by several issuers may help stabilize demand and supply but are not yet sufficient to ensure a recovery of the IHSG. Issuers announcing buybacks include PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) with Rp5 trillion for October 19–21, 2026; PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) with Rp1 trillion from internal cash through January 18, 2027; PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) and PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN) with Rp1 trillion each; PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) with Rp300 billion for October 19–December 31, 2026; and PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) with up to Rp1 trillion for October 20, 2026–January 19, 2027. He noted trading showed some resistance after sell pressure, even as some stocks still fell under the Auto Reject Bottom (ARB) limit of a maximum 7% that took effect on October 19, 2026. Investors are advised to wait and see, raise cash portions, and monitor risks including the potential downgrade of Indonesia to standalone market status in MSCI classification before increasing exposure.
